newsitem.title: BRAZIL: GM to invest $1.25 bln in Brazil.
newsitem.headline: GM to invest $1.25 bln in Brazil.

text.p: The Brazilian subsidiary of General Motors Corp said it would invest $1.25 billion to build three new plants in Brazil.
One plant would be for the manufacture of passenger vehicles and the other two for components, its General Motors do Brasil unit said in a statement.
"This is the biggest sign of our confidence in the country...the stability of the economy and the validity of the current industrial policies for the sector," the company said.
Forty percent of the new investment will be provided by suppliers. GM said the new investment would bring its total investment commitments in Brazil up to the year 2000 to $3.5 billion.
During a meeting with President Fernando Henrique Cardoso, GM do Brasil president Mark Hogan said the company had plans for further expansion, possibly in the north and northeast.
The passenger car factory, to be located in Rio Grande do Sul state, will account for $600 million of the new investment and will produce the Chevrolet line, probably from end-1999.
One of the component plants will be located in Santa Catarina state, involving an investment of $500 million, and will supply existing GM factories in Brazil.
The third new plant, in Sao Paulo state, will cost $150 million and produce body parts.
GM said it would invest $7.5 billion over the next 10 years in the Mercosur customs union.
